Change c0163. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): "She is innocent, my Elizabeth," said I, "and that shall be proved; fear nothing, but let your spirits be cheered by the assurance of her acquittal."

1818 text: "How kind you are! every one else believes in her guilt, and that made me wretched; for I knew that it was impossible: and to see every one else prejudiced in so deadly a manner, rendered me hopeless and despairing."

1831 text: "How kind and generous you are! every one else believes in her guilt, and that made me wretched, for I knew that it was impossible: and to see every one else prejudiced in so deadly a manner rendered me hopeless and despairing."

Diff: " How kind {+and generous+} you are! every one else believes in her guilt, and that made me wretched [-;-] {+,+} for I knew that it was impossible: and to see every one else prejudiced in so deadly a manner [-,-] rendered me hopeless and despairing. "

Context after (unchanged): She wept.

result.rationale: Adds 'and generous' to Justine's praise of Elizabeth's kindness ('How kind and generous you are!'), a stylistic intensifier; the semicolon and comma swaps are punctuation only. Slight shift in how Justine regards Elizabeth.
